actions.intent: Prevent cross-profile working-directory state bleed for equal raw session ids and preserve symmetric cleanup.
actions.pre_state: The cwd map records, reads, and clears by raw session id, so a profile sharing the id can observe or overwrite another profile's directory and can clear its record.
actions.post_state: Record, get, and clear all address the same scope-qualified slot; a different routed profile sees no prior record, owns its own cwd, and can clear only that slot, while no override continues to use the raw slot.
actions.validation: The cwd regression test records profile A's directory, verifies profile B starts empty, records and clears B, and then verifies A remains unchanged; a separate no-override assertion verifies raw map storage.
actions.description: Apply the same routed scope qualification to session working-directory record, lookup, and teardown operations so cwd state cannot cross profile boundaries or be cleared asymmetrically.

actions.intent: Make retry guidance visible at the current context boundary without invalidating or expanding the stable system-instruction prefix.
actions.pre_state: A retry follows a thought-only or no-response-text invalid stream; request contents may end in a model turn, an ordinary user turn, or a function-response user turn, and hooks may replace contents.
actions.post_state: System instruction is unchanged; the retry nudge is present at the end of valid contents, role alternation is preserved with a synthetic model bridge when required, and an existing final-turn nudge is not duplicated.
actions.validation: GeminiChat tests assert unchanged systemInstruction, nudge placement in contents, reapplication after hook-modified contents, handling of empty/model/function-response histories, and deduplication.
actions.description: Place invalid-stream retry guidance at the end of request contents while preserving API role ordering and hook modifications, instead of mutating the stable system instruction.

actions.intent: Make a failed localized edit actionable by distinguishing an exact-match miss and directing the agent to inspect current content.
actions.pre_state: A nonblank edit search string produces zero matches in the current file.
actions.post_state: The tool reports an exact-match failure and advises rereading the target/current lines before retrying; the correction path remains available for valid nonblank input according to its existing policy.
actions.validation: The edit regression test checks that both LLM-facing content and display output contain the new exact-match wording.
actions.description: Replace vague no-occurrence edit feedback with exact-match guidance that points the agent to current file content before retrying.

actions.intent: Keep active tool, code, file, or similar payloads usable while removing empty text artifacts that can trigger request validation failures.
actions.pre_state: An outgoing part has text equal to the empty string, either alongside another active payload or as its only meaningful field.
actions.post_state: The empty text key is removed from payload-bearing parts; text-only empty parts are filtered; other payload-bearing parts remain.
actions.validation: The implementation contains separate payload-preservation and empty-part filtering branches, but no dedicated regression assertion for this newly added sanitizer behavior is present in the pinned commit tests.
actions.description: Normalize outgoing content parts so an empty text field cannot invalidate a payload-bearing part or remain as a truly empty text-only part.

actions.intent: Make the restrictive multi-hook permission contract executable as a regression check.
actions.pre_state: The generic merge behavior had no direct tests for multiple hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision values, so an overwritten deny could pass existing tests.
actions.post_state: The collocated test suite specifies severity precedence, input-order independence, winning-rank reason behavior, single-hook behavior, preservation of unrelated last-wins fields, and no-decision outputs.
actions.validation: The focused hook aggregator tests are the direct oracle: they construct aggregateResults inputs and assert the final PreToolUse decision, reason, and unrelated-field values.
parameters: ordered test sequences of hook outputs
actions.description: Add a focused regression oracle for the structured permission aggregation contract and its compatibility boundary.

actions.intent: Keep provider initialization at the application boundary while preserving construction of the request consumer across all known callers.
actions.module_role: consumer factory interface and its call sites
actions.pre_state: The consumer factory requires provider configuration arguments, and production and tests pass those arguments at every construction site.
actions.post_state: The consumer factory accepts only its functional construction inputs, and known production and test callers use the reduced interface.
actions.validation: Diff all known Coder.create call sites and existing constructor-oriented tests to confirm removal of the obsolete argument; the suite could not be executed locally because dependencies were missing.
actions.description: Remove provider credentials from the consumer factory contract and migrate production and test callers to the configuration-independent constructor.

actions.intent: Apply a compatibility policy only to requests targeting the endpoint whose wire contract requires it, without misrouting other hosts that serve the same model family.
actions.pre_state: The affected endpoint falls through to a generic compatible-provider implementation, while model identifiers are insufficient to identify the actual endpoint.
actions.post_state: Exact canonical hostname and legitimate subdomains select the specialized adapter; unrelated, hostile-suffix, missing, and invalid URLs do not.
actions.validation: Route exact-host, subdomain, and hostile lookalike URLs through provider selection and assert their resulting request behavior distinguishes matched from fallback endpoints.
actions.description: Select an endpoint-specific compatibility adapter using parsed hostname boundaries rather than model-family names or substring matching.

actions.intent: Keep the context breakdown's messages attribution aligned with the active session instead of subtracting another session's cache hit.
actions.pre_state: collectContextData reads total tokens from the active chat but reads cached tokens globally; a foreign positive cache can drive the messages row toward zero.
actions.post_state: The active chat's non-nullish cached count, including zero, drives the cache/messages split; the process-global singleton is used only when the chat value is unavailable.
actions.validation: CLI tests pin both a nonzero active-chat cache against a foreign global cache and an active-chat zero against a foreign global cache; both prevent the approximately 614 leaked messages result.
actions.description: Make context aggregation prefer the active session's cached-content count while retaining a compatibility fallback when no usable chat-local value exists.

actions.intent: Bound each cache-warming provider request to one output token without permanently reducing the normal completion budget or triggering repeated one-token prefill continuations.
actions.module_role: Request-parameter isolation at the boundary between background cache maintenance and foreground model completion.
actions.pre_state: The warming worker aliases the model's extra-parameter mapping, overwrites its max_tokens entry with 1, and the normal send path later consumes that same mapping.
actions.post_state: The warming worker uses a distinct kwargs mapping with max_tokens=1, while the model's extra_params retains its configured entries, such as the normal max_tokens budget, for later requests.
actions.validation: The parent and pinned diff plus the call sites provide a static invariant oracle: the warming completion consumes the copied kwargs while the foreground path still consumes model.extra_params. Existing cache-option tests cover activation only; a mocked-provider regression test for both the one-token warm ping and preserved normal budget is absent.
actions.description: Create request-local cache-warming kwargs before applying the one-token maintenance cap, preserving the model's configured parameters for subsequent foreground and prefill completions.

actions.intent: Prevent cross-profile reuse of a session-isolated sandbox when different profiles generate the same raw API-session fingerprint.
actions.pre_state: For a session-isolated backend, the alias-resolved raw task id is used directly as the environment-cache identity, so identical raw ids from different routed profiles can attach to one sandbox.
actions.post_state: The alias-resolved task identity is prefixed by the active routed scope, making equal raw ids from different profiles distinct; subagent aliases still resolve to the parent's qualified identity, while no routed override keeps the raw key and earlier explicit isolation overrides remain authoritative.
actions.validation: The regression tests prove named-profile qualification, distinct keys for a research/default fingerprint collision, qualified subagent-parent resolution, and raw behavior without an override. The commit also reports live Docker isolation in both profile directions.
actions.description: Namespace the alias-resolved task identity used for a session-isolated sandbox by the active routed profile/home, preventing same-fingerprint profiles from sharing an environment cache slot while preserving subagent aliasing and legacy raw behavior.

actions.intent: Prevent false positives when a non-inspection tool demonstrates progress, when a retry replays a failed attempt, or when a new prompt starts a fresh detection state.
actions.module_role: Loop-detector state lifecycle and false-positive boundary manager
actions.pre_state: The detector has accumulated zero or more recognized inspection calls and receives either another shell request, a non-inspection tool call, a Retry event, or a prompt reset; no earlier always-on detector has already terminated the turn.
actions.post_state: A nonmatching tool call clears the shell bucket and streak before later inspections; Retry and prompt reset clear the shell tracking through the shared tool-call reset; productive write-bearing chains, file-specific diffs, and mixed commands never increment the shell-inspection streak.
actions.validation: Tests assert that seven inspections followed by read_file and seven more do not halt, that a Retry restarts the count, that explicit session disable suppresses the shell guard, and that write-bearing, mixed, non-git, and file-specific command sequences remain below the shell-stagnation detector.
actions.description: Reconcile the inspection streak at progress and lifecycle boundaries so the always-on guard fails open for legitimate work and does not carry state across retries or new prompts.

actions.intent: Remove an unintended fixed token ceiling that makes compression fire at a non-proportional point across heterogeneous context windows, while preserving an explicit user-controlled absolute cost ceiling.
actions.module_role: Compression budget policy and configuration defaulting
actions.pre_state: When compression.threshold_tokens is absent, the defaulted configuration supplies 256000; agent construction passes that value as an absolute cap and the compressor lowers the ratio/model trigger to min(ratio_trigger, 256000).
actions.post_state: When compression.threshold_tokens is absent, the canonical value is None and the effective trigger is the ratio/model-derived threshold with no absolute cap; a positive explicit cap still lowers the trigger and remains durable across model switches.
actions.validation: The changed compressor test covers 128000 and 1000000 context windows and asserts no default cap plus equality with the ratio-only trigger; the explicit-cap test asserts a 200000 cap survives a switch. Gateway-cache and TUI tests verify that consumers use the canonical default and distinguish explicit positive caps.
actions.description: Make the absolute compression-trigger cap opt-in by changing the canonical default and its seeded template from 256000 to null/None, while retaining explicit positive caps as lower-of ratio-versus-absolute controls.

actions.intent: Prevent cancelled in-flight tool turns from persisting as transcript state and avoid unnecessary follow-up work.
actions.pre_state: A prepared query has been sent, the model has appended a tool-call turn, all applicable model-initiated tools are terminally cancelled, and current history is longer than the saved query checkpoint.
actions.post_state: History is truncated to the saved checkpoint; cancellation response parts are not appended and no continuation request is emitted.
actions.validation: Interactive stream regression tests verify that addHistory is not called, history returns to the pre-model length, and the model stream is not called again for one or multiple cancelled tools.
actions.description: When every model-initiated tool in an interactive turn is cancelled, restore the conversation to the checkpoint taken before the current query instead of recording cancellation responses as a new user turn or sending another request.

actions.intent: Reconstruct the correct session-and-route cached value after a route switch or a compression rescue that mutates and then rolls back token state.
actions.pre_state: Route retention reads cached content from the shared telemetry mirror, and hard-rescue rollback restores prompt/output state without an explicit chat-local cached snapshot.
actions.post_state: Each retained route record stores its owning chat's cached count; route adoption and failed hard-rescue rollback restore that count together with prompt/output state and the telemetry mirror.
actions.validation: The core tests recover 42 after switching away and back, and recover 42,000 on the original override route after a failed hard rescue without allowing the active route to inherit it.
actions.description: Carry the cached count through route retention/adoption and failed hard-rescue rollback with the rest of the route-scoped token state.

actions.intent: Give each session an authoritative cached-content count associated with the same chat that owns its prompt total.
actions.pre_state: Prompt and output counts are chat-local, but cached-content usage is available only through a process-global mirror; route retention has no chat-local cached source.
actions.post_state: The chat owns a cached-content count and exposes it through a route-aware getter; retained token-state records can carry the value with the chat's prompt/output counts.
actions.validation: The core route test records cached=42, reads it from the chat, switches routes to observe zero, and returns to the original route to recover 42.
actions.description: Materialize cached-content token usage as first-class state on each chat/session and expose it through a route-aware accessor, rather than making the process-global last-writer value the only source.

actions.intent: Stop a model that keeps inspecting repository state without making progress, including loops that vary command spelling or harmless flags and therefore bypass exact tool-call matching.
actions.module_role: Always-on shell-inspection circuit breaker in the loop-detection service
actions.pre_state: The current event is a run_shell_command request that normalized to the read-only inspection bucket, the current contiguous streak is below eight, and the detector has not already halted the turn.
actions.post_state: When eight contiguous recognized inspection requests arrive while the shell-stagnation detector is active, the service sets loopDetected, records shell_command_stagnation as the last loop type, logs the loop event, and returns true; requests below the threshold return false and continue.
actions.validation: The positive unit test passes seven overview variants without halting and asserts that the eighth sets LoopType.SHELL_COMMAND_STAGNATION and emits telemetry; the reported bundled-CLI verification reproduces the same eighth-call halt before the 100-call cap.
actions.description: Count contiguous semantically equivalent shell inspections and halt the turn on the eighth recognized overview inspection before the generic hard cap is reached.

actions.intent: Avoid incremental declaration-list and prompt-prefix churn for a small deferred set while retaining on-demand discovery for a set that exceeds the budget.
actions.pre_state: Deferred tool schemas are hidden behind discovery, and the registry has no combined footprint decision; bundled and MCP candidates may coexist with already-revealed, visible, or always-loaded tools.
actions.post_state: The registry estimates the union of eligible deferred schemas as ceil(serialized-schema-characters/CHARS_PER_TOKEN) and reveals all eligible unrevealed candidates iff that estimate is within budget; otherwise no candidate is newly revealed. Visible and always-loaded tools are excluded, while already-revealed candidates still count.
actions.validation: Registry tests cover fit, overflow, bundled-plus-MCP all-or-nothing behavior, already-revealed accounting, visible-tool exclusion, and always-loaded exclusion; declaration-path code shows that revealed schemas enter the function-declaration list.
actions.description: Estimate the complete eligible deferred-tool schema union and reveal every candidate only when the combined estimate fits the supplied budget; preserve full deferral on overflow.

actions.intent: Remove the silent unknown-model output fallback for the canonical alias while aligning its output behavior with the already-supported V4 family. [E1,E7,E10]
actions.pre_state: The parent output table recognizes only `/^deepseek-v4/`; `deepseek-flash` matches no DeepSeek output row and consequently returns the 32,000 default, causing output consumers to treat it as an unknown model. [E1,E2,E7]
actions.post_state: The output row returns 384,000 for `deepseek-flash`, the provider sees the model as explicitly known, and the default request follows the existing V4 behavior with a 64,000 ceiling; `deepseek-v3.2`, `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-reasoner`, and `deepseek-chat` remain unchanged. [E3,E10]
actions.validation: The new output assertion passes, and the maintainer A/B records 32000/unknown/32000 before versus 384000/known/64000 after, with the neighboring model rows unchanged. [E5,E8,E10]
actions.description: Extend the output-limit mapping in parallel so `deepseek-flash` receives the V4 384K advertised output limit and follows the existing known-model provider path instead of the 32K unknown-model default. The existing 64K automatic output ceiling remains the request-level cap, and older output rows are preserved. [E1,E2,E3,E7,E10]

actions.intent: Prevent regressions where normalization works in isolation but adapter output still hides or duplicates the provider reason.
actions.pre_state: The shared contract and adapter integrations have been implemented, but their behavior across error shapes and adapter tiers is not yet established.
actions.post_state: Tests specify that output preserves error stop state, includes HTTP status and body reason, excludes known opaque-only output, bounds long bodies, and avoids duplicate supplemental text.
actions.validation: The three added test files provide utility-level and representative adapter-level assertions; the available evidence does not include an executed test or CI result.
actions.description: Exercise utility edge cases and representative real adapter catch paths with opaque SDK messages that retain the actual reason in separate body fields.

actions.intent: Prevent stale nonzero cached metadata from surviving a zero cache report, prompt-state replacement, route invalidation, or fast history compression.
actions.pre_state: The old response path updates the global cached mirror only for nonzero values, while prompt seeding and fast compression reset prompt/output state without resetting a chat-owned cached count.
actions.post_state: A usable prompt/total report writes the coerced cached count onto the chat and telemetry even when zero; prompt seeding, route invalidation, and fast compression clear the cached state consistently with the replaced prompt state.
actions.validation: Core tests cover omitted cached metadata clearing the count, setLastPromptTokenCount clearing it, fast compression clearing it and the telemetry mirror, and metadata-only responses without a usable prompt count remaining unstamped.
parameters: usable prompt or total token-count predicate
actions.description: Synchronize the chat-local and global mirrors from stampable provider usage and clear cached state whenever a fresh prompt count or rewritten history supersedes the old response metadata.

actions.intent: Remove a stale materialized default from existing configuration files so the new policy takes effect after upgrade without clobbering user-selected resource budgets.
actions.module_role: Versioned configuration migration and user-choice preservation
actions.pre_state: A versioned configuration below schema v47 may contain compression.threshold_tokens: 256000 copied from the old template or doctor seeding; the same field may instead contain another explicit positive integer or null.
actions.post_state: The v47 migration deletes the field only when its raw value equals exactly 256000, allowing the new DEFAULT_CONFIG None to apply; other explicit caps, explicit null, and unrelated configuration values remain intact.
actions.validation: The new registry entry and the existing equality-gated deletion helper directly encode the exact-value guard. The generic upgrade property test dynamically includes registered migration versions and checks latest-version convergence, user-value preservation, idempotence, and reapplication stability, but does not directly generate threshold_tokens: 256000.
actions.description: Migrate configurations that persisted the temporary 256000 default so they inherit the new ratio-only default, without rewriting an intentional cap or explicit null.

actions.intent: Ensure a detected shell-inspection loop stops further tool execution and is visible to both structured stream consumers and human users.
actions.module_role: Core stream event consumer and non-interactive diagnostic presenter
actions.pre_state: The streamed model response has produced a tool-call event and the loop detector has set a typed always-on loop outcome.
actions.post_state: When the always-on service returns true, the core client clears pending tool calls, yields LoopDetected with the typed loop reason, reports the error, performs cleanup, and returns; the CLI labels shell_command_stagnation as repeated similar shell inspections and states that model.skipLoopDetection cannot disable this guard.
actions.validation: The head client shows the always-on check before the skipLoopDetection gate and the early-return cleanup path; the CLI maps the new enum value and the reported end-to-end run finishes with shell_command_stagnation after seven tool results and the eighth request.
actions.description: Use the existing always-on stream termination path to discard pending continuation work and present a human-readable, non-disableable halt reason to non-interactive users.

actions.intent: Prevent a tool-execution path from terminating without a user-facing explanation when the first post-tool response is empty.
actions.pre_state: At least one tool call has completed, the next stream has no tool calls, and it emits no non-whitespace content.
actions.post_state: The loop sends the recovery nudge as the next request, clears the armed-after-tool state, and continues; a visible response can then complete the session.
actions.validation: The legacy-session test asserts three stream calls, the exact nudge payload on the third call, tool request/response events, and the final agent message; the non-interactive regression test confirms the additional recovery call.
actions.description: In the session execution loop, recover from an empty response immediately following completed tool calls by sending a dedicated nudge before allowing normal completion.

actions.intent: Demonstrate that replaying a prior thinking turn no longer produces a rejected continuation request.
actions.pre_state: A multi-turn request includes an assistant thought that conversion represents as reasoning_content, and a strict endpoint rejects any assistant reasoning property.
actions.post_state: The continuation receives a successful response, with reasoning_content present and reasoning absent in the captured HTTP request.
actions.validation: Use a strict local HTTP server that returns the reported 400 validation payload if reasoning is present, then execute two turns through OpenAIContentGenerator and inspect the second request body.
actions.description: Exercise the complete history-conversion, provider-adaptation, and HTTP path against a strict contract oracle.

actions.intent: Prevent out-of-range percentage input from turning a bounded preload budget into an oversized or effectively unconditional preload.
actions.pre_state: The new percentage policy can be bypassed by hand-editing or otherwise supplying a value above 100 after static schema validation; the derived budget would otherwise exceed the whole context window.
actions.post_state: Declarative validation accepts only 0-100, and runtime input above 100 is clamped to 100 before token-budget calculation; non-finite and non-positive values still select the no-preload branch.
actions.validation: The generated and source schemas declare minimum 0 and maximum 100, and the client test supplies 200 and asserts a full-context budget rather than a budget above the context window.
actions.description: Defend the percentage invariant at both the declarative settings boundary and runtime so a hand-edited value above 100 cannot allocate a budget larger than the full context window.

actions.intent: Allow one client integration to target provider-compatible endpoints that require additional SDK configuration without embedding startup configuration inside the request consumer.
actions.module_role: application configuration boundary and provider client initializer
actions.pre_state: The application boundary supplies only a key and base, while a downstream consumer factory owns provider SDK mutation and cannot represent type, version, deployment, or engine settings.
actions.post_state: Startup owns provider SDK initialization, exposes the supported endpoint settings, and mutates optional SDK attributes only when corresponding values were supplied.
actions.validation: Inspect parsed option definitions and the pre-construction mapping to provider SDK attributes; verify the downstream factory no longer accepts or assigns provider configuration. Runtime validation remains unavailable in the inspected environment.
actions.description: Accept endpoint-specific provider settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared provider client before constructing downstream consumers.

actions.intent: Identify whether premature compaction is caused by a model-name alias falling into an artificially small or unknown budget bucket. [E1,E10]
actions.pre_state: A provider configuration names a model alias and a long session shows repeated compaction or a compression failure, but the model-name-to-limit mapping has not yet been verified. [E1,E10]
actions.post_state: The probe establishes the before-state contract: `deepseek-flash` resolves to 131072 input, 32000 output, and an unknown-model output classification, while neighboring V4 and older-family identifiers provide comparison controls. [E1,E8,E10]
actions.validation: Run the direct `tokenLimit()` probe and compare it with the issue's measured long-session behavior; the PR's later A/B validation repeats the values and exercises the resulting CLI context/compaction path. [E1,E8,E10]
parameters: observed compression status or context-window behavior [E1,E10]
actions.description: Measure the configured model alias in both input and output dimensions before changing the classifier, so a context-budget failure is distinguished from a compression-algorithm failure. The issue reproduction measured `deepseek-flash` at 131072 input and 32000 output, while the PR validation repeated the same before-state values and compared them with the intended V4 values. [E1,E8,E10]

actions.intent: Translate a percentage resource policy into a concrete token budget before deferred-resource reconciliation.
actions.pre_state: A threshold policy exists, but startup has not derived the number of schema tokens that may be declared up front; explicit context capacity may be absent.
actions.post_state: When deferred discovery is available and the threshold and context are usable, the registry receives floor(contextWindow*boundedThreshold/100); otherwise the budgeted preload call is omitted.
actions.validation: Client tests cover the model-limit fallback at 10%, an explicit 50,000-token context at 10%, threshold 0, non-finite threshold, over-100 input, and missing discovery surface.
actions.description: Convert an accepted positive threshold and available model capacity into a floored token budget at session start, using the configured context window or model-limit fallback and skipping unsupported branches.

actions.intent: Make provider-facing text, response, streaming, and image entry points consistently return actionable HTTP failure details.
actions.pre_state: Adapter catch blocks independently format thrown SDK values, and some lose bodies or duplicate supplemental details.
actions.post_state: Affected adapters consume the shared normalized diagnostic while preserving their established stop reasons, contextual prefixes, exception categories, hints, and nonduplicated supplemental data.
actions.validation: Mocked end-to-end catch-path tests require status and body propagation for representative image, text, response, and Bedrock tiers and require supplemental raw metadata to appear once.
actions.description: Replace adapter-local message-only formatting with the shared diagnostic contract while retaining adapter-specific semantics such as category prefixes, hints, and supplemental metadata.

actions.intent: Recover actionable HTTP failure details that provider SDKs retain outside Error.message.
actions.pre_state: A provider call has thrown an unknown value whose status and body may occupy SDK-specific fields or whose message may already contain the body.
actions.post_state: The failure is represented by a stable record with a safe message, optional numeric status, optional non-empty bounded body, and an explicit body-in-message predicate.
actions.validation: Synthetic error shapes verify field precedence and extraction for multiple SDK conventions, non-Error serialization, empty-body handling, truncation, and existing-body detection.
actions.description: Convert heterogeneous thrown provider values into one bounded diagnostic record containing the original message, optional HTTP status, optional body, and a flag indicating whether the message already carries that body.

actions.intent: Prevent a valid high-context model alias from being misclassified into a smaller context window that drives premature compaction and eventual `COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`. [E1,E6,E10]
actions.pre_state: At parent `156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe`, normalization leaves `deepseek-flash` outside the `/^deepseek-v4/` row; first-match resolution therefore falls through to `/^deepseek/` and returns 131072 input tokens. [E1,E2]
actions.post_state: The input row matches names beginning with `deepseek-v4` or `deepseek-flash` and remains ahead of the generic DeepSeek fallback, so `deepseek-flash` resolves to 1,000,000 input tokens while the tested older families retain their existing rows. [E3,E10]
actions.validation: The added input assertion passes in the 91/91 core test run, and the two-tree CLI check changes `deepseek-flash` from a 131.1k to a 1000.0k context window while the `deepseek-xyz` control remains at 131.1k. [E5,E8,E9,E10]
parameters: custom provider entry without an explicit `contextWindowSize` [E1,E6]
actions.description: Extend the existing ordered input-limit mapping so the official DeepSeek API alias `deepseek-flash` shares the already-defined V4 1M context bucket before the generic 128K fallback. This fixes the custom-provider path that lets `knownTokenLimit` populate an absent `contextWindowSize`, without changing older DeepSeek families. [E1,E2,E3,E4,E6,E10]

actions.intent: Remove silent post-tool turns while bounding automatic recovery work.
actions.pre_state: A continuation after tool execution finishes with no tool calls and no non-whitespace visible text; the current user query has fewer than two automatic nudge attempts.
actions.post_state: A continuation request carrying the recovery nudge is submitted and the per-user-query counter is incremented; no automatic nudge is submitted after the two-attempt budget is exhausted.
actions.validation: The interactive-hook test observes a second send containing the exact recovery nudge after an empty continuation.
actions.description: Recover an interactive continuation that follows tool execution but ends without visible text by issuing a bounded recovery nudge through the normal continuation path.

actions.intent: Recognize semantically equivalent repository-overview inspections even when the model varies the command text, while leaving productive or file-scoped shell work outside the stagnation bucket.
actions.module_role: Shell-command intent classifier inside the loop-detection service
actions.pre_state: A tool-call event contains a tool name and argument object, and the command may be an arbitrary shell string whose semantic intent has not yet been classified.
actions.post_state: For a run_shell_command request, every nonempty shell segment is classified into the stable bucket run_shell_command:git-inspection only when it is a read-only git status, overview-style git diff, or git ls-files inspection; non-git commands, file-specific diffs, write-bearing chains, and mixed shell chains produce no bucket key and follow the reset path.
actions.validation: The service tests exercise varied git status/diff/ls-files commands and newline-separated chains, and assert that file-specific diffs with and without --, add/status/commit chains, mixed non-git chains, and repeated non-git commands are not classified as shell stagnation.
actions.description: Normalize a shell tool request into a semantic read-only repository-inspection bucket so syntactic command variation cannot evade duplicate detection.

actions.intent: Preserve the strongest safety-relevant permission outcome when multiple structured hook results contribute to one tool-execution gate.
actions.pre_state: Multiple matching hook outputs contribute hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision values, but generic last-wins merging lets a later allow or ask replace an earlier deny; the downstream PreToolUse gate consumes the merged hook-specific value.
actions.post_state: The aggregate contains the most restrictive supplied structured permission decision under deny > ask > allow, independent of input order, and exposes only the corresponding winning-rank reason(s), with equal-rank reasons joined in merge order.
actions.validation: Focused aggregateResults tests assert deny dominates allow in both orders, deny dominates ask, ask dominates allow, and the resulting PreToolUse accessors report the expected blocking or confirmation state.
parameters: ordered collection of matching hook outputs
actions.description: Make the structured permission verdict from multiple matching PreToolUse hooks severity-aware so aggregation cannot weaken a restrictive result because of input or configuration order; retain reason information only from the winning rank, joining equal-rank reasons.

actions.intent: Apply the resource decision at the stable startup boundary so preloaded schemas are declared initially and are not later reintroduced as deferred reminders.
actions.pre_state: Startup would resolve deferred reminders without a budget stage, so any preload decision would either be absent from initial declarations or require a later declaration-list change.
actions.post_state: Preload runs after warm/resume reconciliation and before reminder setup; revealed tools are included in the initial declarations and filtered from the deferred reminder, while the existing no-discovery eager-reveal branch and late-registration deferral remain intact.
actions.validation: The client startup call site establishes the stage ordering; reminder and declaration consumers show how revealed state is applied; client tests cover the preload stage and the no-discovery skip branch. No direct prompt-cache measurement is present.
actions.description: Run the budgeted reveal after registry warm/resume handling and before deferred-reminder construction so the initial declaration list and reminder reflect the same revealed state without introducing a mid-session preload mutation.

actions.intent: Prevent strict-schema request rejection without discarding supported replay data, explicit caller intent, or shared history.
actions.pre_state: An inherited generic transformation has added a reasoning field equal to reasoning_content on an assistant history message, but the selected endpoint rejects reasoning and accepts reasoning_content.
actions.post_state: The outbound copy omits reasoning only when it exactly matches the derived mirror signature; reasoning_content and distinct explicit reasoning values remain, and the source request is unchanged.
actions.validation: Assert the mirrored-equality case is removed, unequal explicit values are retained, supported content remains present, source history is not mutated, and fallback providers preserve their prior behavior.
actions.description: At the outbound boundary, remove only a field recognizable as a derived mirror while retaining the endpoint-supported source field and distinct explicit values.

actions.intent: Expose the provider's actual HTTP reason without duplicating it or discarding established adapter context.
actions.pre_state: A normalized failure may contain status and body separately, may already include the body in its message, and may require an adapter-specific prefix.
actions.post_state: The diagnostic contains status plus body when separately available; otherwise it preserves the message, with the requested prefix and status where applicable, and does not print the body twice.

actions.intent: Restore a resumed session on the provider interface most recently used by that session without discarding compatible legacy route metadata.

workflows.exit_state: The model emits visible text after the recovery request or the session follows its normal completion/failure path.

workflows.name: interactive-tool-turn-bounding
workflows.description: The interactive path has two event-dependent recovery branches: remove a cancelled tool turn from durable history, or recover a silent successful tool continuation with a bounded nudge.
workflows.goal: Keep interactive tool turns bounded and recoverable without growing invalid or silent conversation state.
workflows.entry_state: A user query is being processed; the model may request tools, produce an empty continuation, or have all requested tools cancelled.
workflows.exit_state: Cancelled turns are absent from durable history, or a post-tool continuation produces visible completion or stops after the automatic-nudge budget.
unresolved_or_deferred: The two actions are predicate-selected branches of the same coordinator rather than a mandatory sequence: rollback applies to all-cancelled tool turns, while nudging applies to a successful tool continuation with no visible response.
